newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper called to open slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper called to open slightly higher.

text.p: COMEX copper futures were called to open slightly higher Wednesday, with LME three-month copper firmer in London after the February options declaration, traders said.
COMEX March copper was called unchanged to up 0.30 cent from Tuesday's close of 104.00 cents a lb. It traded from 103.90 to 104.50 cents on ACCESS.
COMEX copper stocks fell 392 short tons Tuesday to 17,969 short tons, following an 8,750-tonne fall in LME stocks Tuesday to 200,500 tonnes.
Arbitrage opportunities have drawn copper into LME warehouses over the past two weeks, helping ease the tightness in the prompt market, by allowing cash prices to fall sharply, analysts said.

The LME cash-to-three month spread widened Wednesday morning to $180 a tonne from a low around $111.00 Tuesday, but remains well below the high of $331.00 set Jan 28, while the COMEX March/May spread was little changed Tuesday around 2.70 cents.

In the past three months, copper prices have been recovering steadily from two year lows seen in mid-1996, when, after the Sumitomo scandal, prices fell to levels that restricted the supply of scrap onto the prompt market.
